landing.headline: Care for people. Protect community animals.
landing.subheading: PawGuard helps community programmes keep trustworthy animal vaccination records and coordinate field work — and helps anyone bitten by an animal find what to do next.

one.title: Find or register the animal
one.body: Trained teams search existing records first, so each community animal has one history instead of many scattered notes.

two.title: Record vaccination evidence
two.body: Field teams submit what was given, when and by whom. Nothing counts as verified until a veterinary reviewer checks it.

three.title: See what is known — and what isn't
three.body: Coordinators see verified records, gaps and uncertainty, so the next round of work goes where it is needed.

landing.transparencyTitle: What this site is — and isn't

transparency.one: PawGuard does not diagnose rabies and cannot tell whether an animal is safe.
transparency.two: A vaccination record shows that a vaccine was recorded as given. It is not a guarantee about the animal.
transparency.three: Health guidance on this site is starter content until a qualified local reviewer approves it. Each page shows its source and review status.

landing.releaseNote: This release covers prevention record-keeping. Learning resources and a facility directory are planned for later releases.

help.title: Bitten or scratched by an animal?
help.intro: Act now. Rabies can be prevented with prompt care after an exposure.
help.stepWashBody: Wash the bite or scratch with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes.
help.stepCareBody: Go to a hospital or health centre as soon as you can, even if the wound looks small. A health worker will decide what care you need, which may include vaccination.
help.whyBody: According to the World Health Organization, once rabies symptoms appear the disease is virtually always fatal. Care after an exposure prevents that.
help.call112: National emergency number in India. It connects to police, fire and health emergency services.
help.call15400: National Rabies Helpline. The programme lists it as serving five states/UTs: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam, Puducherry and Delhi. Check whether it covers your area.
help.notDoBody: PawGuard cannot tell you whether an animal has rabies, and you never need to photograph or approach the animal to get help. Your own care does not depend on finding the animal.
help.reviewNotice: Starter guidance. It follows the WHO rabies fact sheet but has not yet been reviewed by a qualified local health professional for your area.

learn.title: Learn
learn.body: Short, reviewed lessons about living safely alongside community animals are planned for a later release. Until then, the guidance for what to do after a bite is available now.
learn.helpLink: What to do after a bite

findCare.title: Find care
findCare.body: A directory of facilities is not connected yet. PawGuard will only list a facility's services when their source and the date they were last confirmed can be shown.
findCare.meanwhileBody: Go to the nearest government hospital or primary health centre, or call 112 in an emergency.
findCare.helpLink: What to do after a bite

about.title: About PawGuard 360
about.body1: PawGuard 360 is a software prototype for community rabies prevention programmes. It is being built to keep animal vaccination records trustworthy, show uncertainty honestly, and help teams coordinate field work.
about.body2: It is not a clinically validated service, it is not endorsed by any government programme, and it has not yet been piloted with a partner organisation.
about.statusBody: Prevention record-keeping for trained teams, in development. Other modules are listed only when they work.

sources.title: Sources and review status
sources.intro: Every piece of health information on this site names its source and whether a qualified local reviewer has approved it.

summary.verifiedExplain: This confirms a vaccine was recorded as given and the evidence was accepted by a veterinary reviewer. It does not mean the animal cannot carry or transmit disease.

stateExplain.verified: Reviewed and accepted. This confirms a vaccine was recorded as given — not that the animal cannot carry or transmit disease.
stateExplain.rejected: The reviewer did not accept this record.
stateExplain.superseded: A corrected record replaced this one. It is kept for the history.

registry.title: Animals
registry.intro: Search this organisation's registry by reference, nickname or description.
registry.results: {count, plural, =0 {No records} one {# record} other {# records}} in this registry
registry.noResultsBody: Try a different spelling or fewer filters. If the animal isn't registered yet, you can register it.
registry.registryNote: This is the organisation's registry, not a census: many animals in an area may not be registered.

profile.createdNext: Next, you can record vaccination evidence or go back to your task.
profile.mergedBanner: This record was merged into {reference}. Use that record for new information.
profile.disputedBanner: This animal's identity is under review. Check details carefully before linking new information.
profile.reportIncorrectHelp: Describe what looks wrong. A reviewer will check the record.
profile.archiveHelp: Archived records stay in the history but are hidden from searches.
profile.historyRestricted: The change history is visible to people with audit access.
profile.reportSent: Thanks — the record is now marked for identity review.

animalForm.title: Register an animal
animalForm.detailsIntro: Record only what you observed. Leave anything you're not sure about as "Unknown".
animalForm.evidenceIntro: A location and photo help others find the same animal. Both are optional.
animalForm.locationDenied: Location not shared. Choose an area instead.
animalForm.locationUnavailable: Your device couldn't provide a location.
animalForm.reviewIntro: Check the details before saving. The profile will be provisional until reviewed.
animalForm.errorSave: The record could not be saved.

upload.purpose: Use photos you already have or take one only where it is safe. Never approach an unfamiliar or worried animal to take a photo.
upload.constraintsImage: JPEG, PNG or WebP · up to 15 MB
upload.constraintsEvidence: Photo or PDF · up to 15 MB each
upload.pending: Saved. It will be checked shortly — you can continue.

reasons.type_mismatch: the file type doesn't match its contents

upload.failed: Upload failed. Check your connection and try again.

vaccForm.title: Record vaccination evidence
vaccForm.whatNext: What happens next: a veterinary reviewer will check this record. Until then it shows as "Submitted for review".
vaccForm.productNotListed: Not in the list — type the name
vaccForm.lotNotListed: Type the lot number as written
vaccForm.noteHint: Anything the reviewer should know. Do not include personal contact details.
vaccForm.evidenceHint: Optional, but records with evidence are easier to verify.
vaccForm.unknownAllowed: Fields can be left as "Not known" — the reviewer will see that.

conflictRules.possible_duplicate_vaccination: Another record for this animal is dated close to this one.
conflictRules.lot_expired_at_administration: The lot's recorded expiry date is before the administration date.
conflictRules.product_species_mismatch: The product is not recorded as applicable to this species.

review.title: Verification workbench
review.intro: Records waiting for a veterinary reviewer, oldest first. Your own submissions are not shown.
review.verifyExplain: Verifying confirms a vaccine was recorded as given based on the evidence. It does not certify that the animal cannot carry or transmit disease.

done.needs_correction: Correction requested. The submitter has a task to fix it.

review.notAuthorised: Reviewing needs an approved veterinary authority in this organisation.
review.staleRow: Someone else reviewed or changed this record. The queue has been refreshed.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.emptyMine: Field tasks are assigned by your programme coordinator.

merge.title: Possible duplicate
merge.intro: Compare the two records. Merging moves sightings, vaccination records, tasks and caregiver links to the record you keep. It can be reversed.
merge.source: Record to merge (will become an alias)
merge.findTarget: Reference of the record to keep
merge.reason: Why are these the same animal?
merge.proposed: Merge proposed. A different reviewer must approve it.

states.proposed: Proposed — waiting for a second person

merge.secondPerson: You proposed this merge, so someone else must approve it.
merge.notFound: No record with that reference in this organisation.

map.title: Map and areas
map.intro: Sightings and open tasks in this organisation's registry. This is not a disease-risk map.
map.precisionApprox: Locations are approximate (~500 m) for your role.
map.noBasemap: No basemap is configured; areas and points are drawn without background map tiles.
map.registryNote: Registry measures, not population coverage: animals that were never registered are not counted.
map.truncated: Only the 2,000 most recent sightings are shown.
map.showList: The table below lists the same information.

capture.title: Add a photo or sighting
capture.intro: Record where and when you saw an animal you have already found in the registry.
capture.matchingUnavailableBody: PawGuard cannot yet suggest which registered animal a photo shows. Find the animal in the registry first (by reference, nickname or description), then add the sighting from its profile — or register it if it's new.
capture.findFirst: Find the animal in the registry
capture.notesHint: What you observed (no medical judgements, no personal contact details).
capture.lookupTitle: Find an animal from a photo
capture.lookupIntro: Suggestions help you find the right record faster. You decide; nothing is linked automatically.

subject.checking: Looking for animals in the photo…
subject.photoAlt: Your photo with possible animals marked
subject.whichDog: Several dogs may be in this photo. Which one is this record about?
subject.isThisTheDog: Is this the dog this record is about?
subject.noneOfTheseHint: The photo is kept without marking a dog.
subject.noDogFound: No dog was found automatically. You can still use this photo.
subject.detectionUnavailable: Automatic detection isn't available right now. You can still use this photo.
subject.personBody: Photos are private to your organisation, but avoid photos where people can be recognised.
subject.detectionOnly: Boxes only show where a dog may be. They do not identify the animal or say anything about its health.
subject.qualityTitle: This photo may be hard to use
subject.overrideHint: For example: it is the only photo available. Required to continue with this photo.

warnings.subject_small: The animal is small in the frame.
warnings.overexposed: The photo is very bright or washed out.

subject.whichDogLookup: Which dog do you want to look up?

imports.title: Data imports
imports.intro: Bring in records from a partner's spreadsheet. Every file is checked first; nothing is created until you apply it.
imports.uploadIntro: Upload a UTF-8 CSV file (up to 2 MB). You will see a row-by-row report before anything changes.

types.vaccinations_csv: Vaccination records (arrive as submitted for review)

columns.animals_csv: Columns: source_row_id (required), nickname, species, sex, sterilisation_status, age_band, ownership_category, area_code, last_seen_date, latitude, longitude, coat_description, identifying_marks.
columns.vaccinations_csv: Columns: source_row_id and animal_reference (required), administered_on, date_precision, product_name, lot_number, administered_by_name, registration.

imports.sourceHint: For example: "Partner shelter export, September". Kept with every imported record.
imports.dateFormat: Date format used in the file
imports.fileHint: Values are trimmed and mapped to PawGuard's vocabulary; unclear values are flagged, never guessed.
imports.labelRequired: Say where the file is from.
imports.failed: The file could not be checked.
imports.notAppliedBody: Review the rows below. Rejected rows and rows imported before are never applied. Possible matches with existing records are only hints — a reviewer decides about merges.
imports.apply: Apply {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}
imports.applyConfirm: Create records from {count, plural, one {# row} other {# rows}}?
imports.applyExplain: Records are created in one step and marked with this import. Animal profiles start as provisional; vaccination records arrive as "submitted for review".
imports.rollbackExplain: Records that nobody has used since the import are archived (kept for the history, hidden from searches). If any were used, roll back is refused.

identity.previewBody: This demo organisation can try photo-based suggestions from a research model. It has only been tested on a research set of dog face photos, not on community dogs in the field. It is not offered for real records. Always compare the photos and details yourself.
identity.step1: 1. Add a photo and choose the animal in it
identity.chooseSubjectFirst: Choose which animal in the photo you mean before searching.
identity.tookTooLong: The search is taking longer than expected. Search the registry instead, or try again later.
identity.noneNew: None of these — register a new animal
identity.notSureSaved: Saved as "not sure". Nothing was linked. You can search the registry or ask a colleague.
identity.confirmTitle: Record this photo as a sighting of {ref}?
identity.confirmBody: Only confirm if the photos and details clearly show the same animal. The sighting is saved with today's date; you can add details from the profile.
identity.completedBody: These are animals whose photos look similar. They are suggestions, not identifications — similar-looking dogs are common. If none is clearly the same animal, choose "None of these" or "Not sure".
identity.noCandidateBody: No photo among the {n} animals with photos on record looked similar enough. This does not prove the animal is new — search the registry by description before registering.
identity.staleBody: Some recent photos have not been added to the comparison yet, so a matching animal could be missing. Search the registry as well.
identity.qualityTitle: The chosen area is too small to compare
identity.qualityBody: Choose the animal in a closer or clearer photo, or search the registry by description.
identity.failedTitle: Photo comparison didn't work this time
identity.failedBody: Search the registry by reference, nickname or description, or register the animal. Nothing was linked.
identity.researchOnly: A research model exists, but it has not passed validation on field photos, so it is not offered for real records.

field.setupRisk: Anyone who can use this device while it is unlocked could see them. Do not use a shared or public device.
field.setupNotStored: Not saved here: photos, caregiver details, exact locations or vaccination records. Vaccination evidence still needs a connection.
field.enable: Use this device for field work
field.needsConnection: You need a connection and to be signed in to set this up.
field.prepared: Ready. {n, plural, one {# task is} other {# tasks are}} saved on this device.

prepareError.signedOut: Sign in first, then open the field kit again.
prepareError.failed: The tasks could not be downloaded. Try again when the connection is better.
prepareError.otherAccountPending: This device holds unsent changes from another account or organisation. Send or discard them first.

field.stopped: Offline data was removed from this device.
field.savedUntil: Saved for offline use until {date}. Refresh while online to keep it current.
field.stop: Stop using this device for field work
field.waitingToSend: {n, plural, one {# change is} other {# changes are}} saved on this device and will be sent when you are online.
field.stillOffline: Still offline. Your changes are kept on this device.
field.signInToSend: Sign in again to send your changes. They are kept on this device.
field.accessEnded: Your access to this organisation has changed, so the changes could not be sent. Ask your coordinator.
field.sendFailed: Sending failed. Your changes are kept; try again shortly.
field.sentSummary: Sent: {accepted} applied, {conflicts, plural, one {# needs} other {# need}} a decision, {rejected} not accepted.
field.expiredBody: Tasks older than 72 hours were removed from this device. Refresh while online.
field.conflictBody: Someone changed this task while you were offline. It is now: {state}. Nothing was overwritten.
field.applyToLatest: Apply my change to the latest version
field.noTasks: No open tasks are assigned to you.
field.notOffline: Registering animals, photos and vaccination evidence need a connection.
field.sightingExplain: Saved with today's date and the task's area. Photos can be added later from the animal's profile.
field.stopTitle: Remove offline data from this device?
field.stopBody: Saved tasks and settings for offline work are deleted from this device.
field.stopWithPending: {n, plural, one {# change has} other {# changes have}} not been applied yet and will be lost.
field.signOutPendingTitle: {n, plural, one {# change made offline was} other {# changes made offline were}} not sent
field.signOutPendingBody: Signing out removes offline data from this device, including these changes. Open the field kit to send them first.

survey.title: Record a street count
survey.intro: Count the dogs you see in the area during this visit. Counts help plan doses and teams.
survey.notCensus: A count is what you saw, not a census. It becomes the suggested estimate for planning this area.
survey.notMoreThanDogs: Cannot be more than the dogs counted.

campaigns.title: Campaign planning
campaigns.intro: Plan field days: which team visits which areas, in what order, within shifts, access times and doses.
campaigns.name: Name
campaigns.needNameAndAreas: Give the campaign a name and choose at least one area.
campaigns.plannerIntro: Set what you know about each area, choose the teams, then make a plan. A plan is a proposal: nothing is sent to teams until you approve and publish it.
campaigns.inputsIntro: Enter your own estimate, or use the suggestion: the latest street count for the area, otherwise the number of registered animals there.
campaigns.speedHint: Used for a straight-line travel estimate; no road routing is configured.
campaigns.noTeams: No teams yet. Add teams before planning.
campaigns.overridesHint: Keep an area with one team, or leave it out. These are respected in every new version.
campaigns.failedTitle: The plan could not be made
campaigns.failedBody: Check the inputs and try again. Teams can still be assigned tasks by hand.
campaigns.proposalBody: Check it with the teams. Times are estimates and animal numbers are planning estimates; nothing is sent until you approve and publish.

reason.no_location: The area has no map location, so travel cannot be estimated.
reason.no_animals_estimated: No animals are expected there yet (add a count or an estimate).
reason.pinned_team_not_in_plan: It is kept for a team that is not in this plan.
reason.longer_than_any_shift: The work there takes longer than any team's shift — split the area or plan more days.
reason.needs_more_doses_than_any_team: It needs more doses than any team carries.
reason.cannot_fit_in_access_window_and_shift: Its access times do not fit any team's shift.
reason.not_enough_time_or_doses_left: Teams' time or doses ran out on higher-priority or closer areas.

campaigns.approveBody: Approval records that you checked it. It does not send anything to teams yet.
campaigns.publishTitle: Create {n, plural, one {# task} other {# tasks}} for the teams?
campaigns.publishBody: Each planned stop becomes a task assigned to its team, with the planned times. Tasks from earlier versions stay as they are.
campaigns.publishedTasks: {n, plural, one {# task was} other {# tasks were}} created.
campaigns.suggestedRegistry: Suggested {n}: registered animals with this home area
campaigns.estimatesBody: A street count is what one person saw on one day: it can miss animals and count some twice. Registry numbers include only registered animals. Only the latest count is used — counts are never added up. These numbers schedule time and doses; they are not population sizes or vaccination coverage.
